title: 3.1 Taste and Odour Receptors
description: How taste and smell receptors detect flavour compounds — the steps of perception, how the signal reaches the brain, and the roles of saliva, memory, and reward in how we experience taste and aroma.

title: 3.2 Impact of Oral Processing Behaviour and Physiology
description: How chewing, saliva, and individual oral physiology shape the way flavour is released and perceived while eating — and why the same food can taste different from one person to the next.

title: 4.1 Static and Dynamic Sensory Methods
description: An overview of sensory evaluation methods — the static and dynamic techniques used to measure how people perceive a food's flavour, including how that perception changes over the course of a bite.

title: 4.2 Static and Dynamic Flavour Analytics
description: Instrumental analytical methods — the static and dynamic techniques used to identify and quantify the key aroma compounds responsible for a food's flavour.
